pluss::timeline::unite¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::unite(timeline_range values)

The input may be a contiguous range of Timelines or a braced list.

Assemble One Sequence In Argument Order¶

unite() appends the logical values of two or more Timelines in operand order and returns one rank-one Timeline. Each operand is flattened in row-major logical order before the next operand begins. It is sequence assembly, not stacking along a selected axis, and there is no dimension parameter.

This distinction is important for shaped input. Joining two 2 x 2 Timelines does not produce 2 x 4, 4 x 2, or 2 x 2 x 2; it produces a vector of eight instants. If a higher-rank arrangement is required, assemble the epoch ticks in that shape deliberately and construct with from_epoch(flat, sizes).

With exactly one operand, unite() is an identity operation: it returns a cheap Timeline handle to the same logical value and preserves the operand’s rank and shape. It does not flatten or allocate a redundant join buffer. The observable flattening contract begins with two operands.

Timezone, Absence, And Empty Inputs¶

Every operand must carry exactly the same timezone label. Matching epoch nanoseconds are not enough: the result has one display zone, so silently choosing the first operand’s metadata would make output depend on argument order. Convert zones explicitly before joining.

Absent instants are retained in position. Empty Timelines are valid operands. When two or more empty operands are joined, the result is an empty rank-one Timeline because multi-input assembly always flattens. An empty operand list is not meaningful and is rejected.

For two or more operands, the output owns newly allocated contiguous storage; changes to any external buffer from which an operand was constructed cannot change the joined result. Logical iteration is respected, so strided operands are copied in their visible order rather than read as if contiguous.

Example 1: Append A Scalar To A Vector¶

const auto result = pluss::timeline::unite({
    pluss::timeline::date({"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"}),
    pluss::timeline::date("2024-01-03")});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(result, "%F")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-03"]

Example 2: Multiple Operands Flatten¶

const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::date({
    {"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"},
    {"2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"}});
const auto result = pluss::timeline::unite({matrix, matrix});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(result, "%F")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[8], dim=1, numel=8, encoding=utf8)
["2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-04", "2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"]

Example 3: One Operand Retains Shape¶

const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::date({
    {"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"},
    {"2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"}});
const auto identity = pluss::timeline::unite({matrix});

std::cout << (identity.sizes() == matrix.sizes()) << '\n';
std::cout << identity.epoch_nanos().equal(matrix.epoch_nanos()) << '\n';

Output¶

true
true

Example 4: Empty Operands Produce An Empty Vector¶

const auto empty = pluss::timeline::unite({
    pluss::timeline::epoch({0, 2}),
    pluss::timeline::epoch({3, 0})});
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(empty) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[0], tz=UTC)[  ]

The two input shapes are different, but both contribute zero flattened values.

Example 5: Absence Keeps Its Position¶

const auto result = pluss::timeline::unite({
    pluss::timeline::make({"2024-01-01", ""}),
    pluss::timeline::date("2024-01-02")});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(result, "%F")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["2024-01-01", "NaT", "2024-01-02"]

Failures And Cost¶

unite() throws for an empty operand range or any timezone-label mismatch. For multiple operands it performs one logical read per input element and one output write, so time and storage are linear in the total numel(). The single-operand identity path is constant-time handle copying.

See Also¶

  • from_epoch: construct an explicitly shaped result from assembled ticks.

  • select: choose values positionally instead of appending them.
